target.title: Remove menu bar icon hover labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Remove hover tooltips from the primary and split/custom menu bar status items.
- Keep the existing accessibility titles for VoiceOver.
- Add regression coverage for standard, split, and custom menu bar layouts.

## Why

CodexBar was the only menu bar item in the reported setup that displayed a text label on hover. Removing that transient tooltip makes the status icon behave consistently with macOS system menu extras and common third-party menu bar apps.

## Root cause

Both status-item creation and custom menu bar layout rendering explicitly copied the accessibility label into `NSStatusBarButton.toolTip`. AppKit then displayed that value as the hover label.

## User impact

Hovering over CodexBar's menu bar icon no longer displays a `CodexBar` label. The menu remains clickable, and assistive technologies retain the same accessibility title.

## Validation

- `make test` — 717 selections passed across all 60 groups with no retries or failures.
- `make check` — SwiftFormat clean and SwiftLint reported zero violations.
- Manual macOS UI verification — the locally built app no longer displayed the hover label, and clicking the status icon still opened the menu normally.

## Visual verification

Before: hovering displayed a transient `CodexBar` tooltip beneath the menu bar icon.

After: no tooltip is displayed. Because the change removes a transient overlay, there is no meaningful static after-state screenshot beyond the unchanged menu bar icon.

target.title: Simplify cost labels and clarify estimate provenance
target.body: ## Summary Simplify cost navigation labels and move the general cost explanation from the menu into Cost settings. - Rename provider cost buttons and sections to the consistent label `Cost` - Move the general reported-versus-estimated explanation to the bottom of Cost settings - Keep one short Codex-specific note beside its displayed values: `Estimated from token usage · not a subscription bill` - Remove repeated explanations and obsolete localized labels from menu and chart views - Keep the CLI label explicit because CLI output has no surrounding UI context ## Why The previous menu mixed navigation labels with explanations such as “API-equivalent estimate” and “Token-based cost estimate.” This caused three problems: 1. The labels were long and frequently truncated. 2. The same Cost destination had different names depending on the provider. 3. A single estimate-focused label was not accurate for every provider: some costs are provider-reported, while others are calculated from token usage. A button should clearly describe where it leads, so all provider buttons now use the concise label `Cost`. Moving the general explanation out of the menu also lets cost entries with submenus use a standard native menu row instead of a custom multi-line SwiftUI card. This restores consistent menu sizing, highlighting, and interaction behavior. The general explanation applies to the Cost feature as a whole, not to one menu item. It now appears in Cost settings, where users can see that values may be provider-reported or estimated from token usage at public API prices, and that estimates are not subscription charges. Codex keeps a short explanation directly under its dashboard details because its prominent dollar values are token-derived and could otherwise be mistaken for an actual bill. This provides the necessary context without repeating the full explanation throughout the menu. The CLI retains `Codex token-based cost` because terminal output must explain itself without relying on the menu or settings UI. ## Result The menu is shorter and more consistent, while the distinction between reported costs, token-derived estimates, and subscription billing remains available where users need it. ## Validation - Focused cost, menu, settings, CLI, and localization tests: 134 passed - `make test`: all 718 selections passed - `make check` - `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` ## Screenshot before after


target.title: Allow up to six Overview providers
target.body:
## Summary

- raise the shared merged Overview provider limit from three to six
- keep selection persistence, reconciliation, chooser copy, and menu rendering aligned with the shared cap
- update the UI documentation to describe the six-provider limit

## Why

The existing three-provider cap prevents users who monitor several AI providers from including them in the merged Overview. Six providers offers a more useful upper bound while preserving the current provider-row presentation and ordering behavior.

This addresses the provider-cap portion of #2107. The compact-density mode and secondary-window disclosure proposed there remain out of scope for this PR.

## User impact

Users can select and persist up to six providers in **Settings → Menu Bar → Overview providers**. When six are selected, additional providers remain unavailable until one of the selected providers is deselected.

## Validation

- `make check` — passed; documentation links, SwiftFormat, SwiftLint, locales, packaging, and repository checks are clean
- `make test` — all 716 selections passed in 60/60 groups with no failures, retries, or timeouts
- focused settings and menu suites — passed
- manual packaged-app verification — the requester confirmed the chooser displays a six-provider maximum and works correctly with the local build

## Visual verification

The updated chooser and six-provider selection boundary were manually verified in the packaged macOS app. No compact-layout changes are included.

target.title: Fix StepFun login web ID
target.body:
## Summary

- derive the StepFun login web ID from the anonymous token before building the Cookie header
- add a regression assertion for the complete password-login Cookie header

## Root cause

The login request interpolated `self.webID`, which is a function reference after `webID(forToken:)` was introduced. Swift emitted a warning and the resulting Cookie header could contain a function debug description instead of the required web ID.

## Impact

Password-based StepFun fallback login now sends a valid `Oasis-Webid` value and the production build no longer emits the function-interpolation warning.

## Validation

- `swift test --filter StepFunTokenRefreshTests` — 8 tests passed
- `swift build -c release` — passed without the StepFun warning
- `make check` — passed
